scientific_question: Does the newly observed midpoint-defined high-threshold equal-class Brier pattern survive uncertainty in recorded ML probabilities and threshold membership?
population: Same four frozen saved joins, original N eligible and O explicit, both releases separate, all constructs. This does not identify missing native scores or performance on N/all molecules.
selection: Symmetric max(q,1-q)>=t only. t=0.5 is the O baseline. No new threshold, optimum selection, one-sided sweep or new resampling.
interval_model: Each explicit prequantization model score q, not biological true probability, is constrained by the existing marginal ML interval [m/256,(m+1)/256). No extra cross-record/cross-modification constraints are imposed. Envelopes are conservative if further constraints exist; no stochastic independence assumption, confidence interval, new statistical-method or model ranking claim.

layers.midpoint_reference: Copy prior midpoint-defined counts and metrics with exact hash/selector and reconcile newly read histograms
layers.fixed_membership: Keep S chosen by recorded midpoint, vary only q within original ML intervals. Use endpoint infima/suprema for class, observed and equal-class Brier; these do not enforce latent q selection on fixed S
layers.variable_membership: For each bin intersect its half-open interval with q<=1-t or q>=t. Distinguish mandatory, optional and impossible retention. For retained q compute loss infimum/supremum on the actual retained intersection; count of selected optional records can be any integer 0..n. Optimize mean loss with its selected denominator, not only total loss or all-in/all-out scenarios

ratio_optimization: For each bound combine mandatory endpoint loss totals with optional-bin endpoint losses. Sort optional-bin endpoint losses ascending for infimum or descending for supremum. Starting with mandatory records, include the whole next bin only if it improves the current ratio. Along a single equal-loss bin the derivative has fixed sign, so an optimum is at zero/all counts (ties immaterial). If no mandatory records, bound the nonempty-selected estimand and explicitly flag possible empty selection. Empty feasible selection is not silently made estimable.
weights: Observed selected composition, 1/2 per class, and original 1/K per construct with 1/2 within class. Original K=5/32. Any required class lacking guaranteed nonzero retention flags potential undefined estimate; do not drop groups or silently renormalize.
contrasts: All six adjacent threshold comparisons and every threshold against t=0.5, with all results retained. Lower_next-upper_previous>tol certifies increase; upper_next-lower_previous<-tol certifies decrease. Otherwise NOT_CERTIFIED_BY_MARGINAL_ENVELOPES. Separate per-threshold envelopes ignore coupling of the same q across thresholds, so overlap never proves a feasible reversal or equality.
decomposition: For ALL truth-class decomposition versus t=0.5, form conservative interval-arithmetic enclosures for within-class and class-weight terms using marginal class-loss and selected-class-weight ranges. Report sign/dominance only if strictly separated under tol. These component ranges are not sharp joint bounds and their endpoints must not be added as a decomposition identity. Reconcile exact midpoint terms with the original result.
missingness: Existing N and O stay fixed, eligible omitted scores stay missing. No inferred historical omission threshold, deletion/base mismatch promotion or zero filling.
item2: Re-present the existing five 2025 construct curves for all seven thresholds in readable Markdown and machine-readable source table with hashes/selectors. Show provider-condition truth and scored denominators. No leave-one-construct-out, no significance test, no biological-replicate interpretation. Reused values are labelled REUSED_PRIOR_RESULT, not new independent evidence.
